plan_a_advantages: Includes threshold hill work for power development
Features a dedicated long run for endurance
More varied workout types (hills, easy runs, long run)
plan_b_advantages: Potentially less taxing on the body due to fewer hard days
Prioritizes form, which is always beneficial for running technique
reasoning: Plan A is the superior training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates targeted hill work at threshold intensity, crucial for building the climbing strength and power necessary for trail running. Furthermore, it includes a longer, controlled endurance run, which is vital for sustained performance on longer trails. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost exclusively on easy runs with a heavy emphasis on form, neglecting the specific physiological adaptations needed for speed and trail-specific demands. While form work is important, it shouldn't overshadow the need for structured, challenging workouts.
